messages.subject: conditional normal
parts:
Hi, everyone. I have three variables (beta, delta, zeta) which follow a tri-variate normal distribution. But now values of one variables zeta is given, and I want to get the sample and estimation of others - beta and delta. I tried the code below, but I am not sure if this  is the right way to achive this. Could you help me to see this? Thanks!





library(data.table)
library(scales)
library(MCMCvis)
library(nimble)
library(MASS)
library(writexl)
library(readxl)
library(grid)


Q=data.frame(matrix(ncol = 7,nrow = 30))
Q[1,]=c(1,0,0,0,0,0,0)
Q[2,]=c(0,1,0,0,0,0,0)
Q[3,]=c(0,0,1,0,0,0,0)
Q[4,]=c(0,0,0,1,0,0,0)
Q[5,]=c(0,0,0,0,1,0,0)
Q[6,]=c(0,0,0,0,0,1,0)
Q[7,]=c(0,0,0,0,0,0,1)
Q[8,]=c(1,0,0,0,0,0,0)
Q[9,]=c(0,1,0,0,0,0,0)
Q[10,]=c(0,0,1,0,0,0,0)
Q[11,]=c(0,0,0,1,0,0,0)
Q[12,]=c(0,0,0,0,1,0,0)
Q[13,]=c(0,0,0,0,0,1,0)
Q[14,]=c(0,0,0,0,0,0,1)
Q[15,]=c(1,1,0,0,0,0,0)
Q[16,]=c(0,0,1,1,0,0,0)
Q[17,]=c(0,0,0,1,1,0,0)
Q[18,]=c(0,0,1,0,0,1,1)
Q[19,]=c(0,0,0,1,1,1,0)
Q[20,]=c(0,1,0,0,1,1,0)
Q[21,]=c(0,0,1,1,0,0,1)
Q[22,]=c(1,0,1,0,0,0,1)
Q[23,]=c(0,1,1,1,0,1,0)
Q[24,]=c(1,1,0,0,1,1,0)
Q[25,]=c(1,1,1,1,0,0,0)
Q[26,]=c(0,0,0,1,1,1,1)
Q[27,]=c(1,1,0,0,1,0,1)
Q[28,]=c(1,1,1,0,0,1,1)
Q[29,]=c(1,0,1,0,1,1,1)
Q[30,]=c(1,1,0,1,1,0,1)

y=fread("JRT_response.csv")
logT=fread("LogTime.csv")
setDF(y)
setDF(logT)


JRT_summary_phi<-read_excel("1_DINA_summary_phi.xlsx")
JRT_summary_Sigma_epsilon<-read_excel("1_DINA_summary_Sigma_epsilon.xlsx")
JRT_summary_sigma_tau<-read_excel("1_DINA_summary_sigma_tau.xlsx")
JRT_summary_zeta<-read_excel("1_DINA_summary_zeta.xlsx")


phi_estimate=JRT_summary_phi$`50%`
den_epsilon_estimate=1/JRT_summary_Sigma_epsilon$`50%`
sigma_tau_estimate=JRT_summary_sigma_tau$`50%`
zeta_estimate=JRT_summary_zeta$`50%`

#start the model
code=nimbleCode({
  for (n in 1:1000) {
    for (i in 1:30) {
      for (k in 1:7) {w[n, i, k] <- pow(attribute[n, k], Q[i, k])}
      logit(prob[n, i]) <- beta[i] + delta[i] * prod(w[n, i, 1:7])
      y[n, i] ~ dbern(prob[n, i])
      logT[n, i] ~ dnorm(zeta[i] - sigma_tau*(theta[n]*sin(phi)+tau[n]*cos(phi)), den_epsilon[i])
    }}
  for (n in 1:1000) {
    for (k in 1:7) {
      logit(att_prob[n, k]) <- gamma[k] * theta[n] - lambda[k]
      attribute[n, k] ~ dbern(att_prob[n, k])
    }}
 
  for (n in 1:1000) {theta[n] ~ dnorm(0,1)}
  for (n in 1:1000) {tau[n] ~ dnorm(0,1)}
  for (i in 1:30) {
    item_parameter[i, 1:3] ~ dmnorm(item_mu[1:3], item_den[1:3, 1:3])
    beta[i] <- item_parameter[i, 1]
    delta[i] <- item_parameter[i, 2]
    zeta[i] <- item_parameter[i, 3]
  }
  for (k in 1:7) {
    lambda[k] ~ dnorm(0, 0.25)#(0,0.25)
    gamma[k] ~ T(dnorm(0, 0.25),0,)#(0,0.25)
  }
  item_mu[1] ~ dnorm(-2.197, 0.25)#(-2.197, 0.5)
  item_mu[2] ~ T(dnorm(4.394, 0.25),0,)#(4.394, 0.5)
  item_mu[3] ~ dnorm(3,0.25)#(3,0.5)
  R[1, 1] <- 1
  R[2, 2] <- 1
  R[3, 3] <- 1
  R[1, 2] <- 0
  R[1, 3] <- 0
  R[2, 1] <- 0
  R[2, 3] <- 0
  R[3, 1] <- 0
  R[3, 2] <- 0
  item_den[1:3, 1:3] ~ dwish(R[1:3, 1:3], 3)
  Sigma_item[1:3, 1:3] <- inverse(item_den[1:3, 1:3])
})

data <- list(y=y,Q=Q,logT=logT,
             phi=phi_estimate,
             sigma_tau=sigma_tau_estimate,
             zeta=zeta_estimate,
             den_epsilon=den_epsilon_estimate)
inits <- list(item_den = diag(3))
monitors=c("gamma","lambda","beta","delta")
model<-nimbleModel(code,data = data,inits=inits)
cModel_JRT <-compileNimble(model)
conf_JRT <- configureMCMC(model, monitors = monitors)
model_JRTMCMC <- buildMCMC(conf_JRT)
cModel_JRTMCMC <- compileNimble(model_JRTMCMC, project = model)
system.time(samples_JRT<-runMCMC(cModel_JRTMCMC, nchains=2,niter = 10000, nburnin = 5000))
